title: feat(automation): accept a per-kernel scheduledWorkPolicy in the engine and both schedule triggers
body:
Closes #19834

Clause-②: no

This PR follows the ruled shape on #19834 (ruling batch #216 item 1, letter ①′, on objectstack-ai/cloud#2337). A kernel can now carry its own `ScheduledWorkPolicy`. The deployment default and its spelling (`OS_AUTOMATION_SCHEDULED_WORK_ENABLED`) are unchanged, and so is `objectstack serve`.

## What changed

| Surface | Change |
|:--|:--|
| `AutomationEngineOptions` (`@objectstack/service-automation`) | New optional `scheduledWorkPolicy`, which takes a `ScheduledWorkPolicy` value or a resolver. The bind gate in `activateFlowTrigger` reads it through a private `readScheduledWorkPolicy()`. When the option is absent, that method calls the zero-argument `resolveScheduledWorkPolicy()` exactly as before. A resolver is called at each bind. |
| `AutomationServicePluginOptions` | New optional `scheduledWorkPolicy`, passed to the engine unchanged. `maxLogSize` and `runSummaryLog` are forwarded the same way. |
| `ScheduleTriggerPlugin`, `TimeRelativeTriggerPlugin` (`@objectstack/trigger-schedule`) | New constructor `options` with an optional `scheduledWorkPolicy`, passed to the trigger they register. `new XPlugin()` behaves as before. |
| `ScheduleTrigger`, `TimeRelativeTrigger` | New trailing constructor argument `options` with `scheduledWorkPolicy`. Each trigger's own gate reads it, and falls back to the deployment resolver when it is absent. |
| Barrel | New exported types: `ScheduleTriggerPluginOptions`, `TimeRelativeTriggerPluginOptions`, `ScheduledWorkTriggerOptions`, `ScheduledWorkPolicySource`. |

The refusal is still structured. A time-triggered flow that the per-kernel policy leaves unarmed gets `SCHEDULED_WORK_DISABLED_REASON` on `getTriggerBindingAudit()` and on its `getFlowRuntimeStates()` row. The engine checks the policy before it looks up the trigger, as before, so the diagnostic names the policy and never says "add `requires: ['triggers']`".

### Every bare call site, re-checked on this tree (`afc3b64928`)

| Site | Disposition |
|:--|:--|
| `service-automation/src/engine.ts` `activateFlowTrigger` | Reads the per-kernel option when one is given, otherwise the deployment resolver. |
| `trigger-schedule/src/schedule-trigger.ts` `ScheduleTrigger.start` (via `readScheduledWorkPolicy`) | Reads the per-kernel option when one is given, otherwise the deployment resolver. |
| `trigger-schedule/src/time-relative-trigger.ts` `TimeRelativeTrigger.start` | Reads the per-kernel option when one is given, otherwise the deployment resolver. On this tree there is one resolver call. It is read once per bind, and the `sweep` closure reuses the result for `runOwnership` and `describeScheduleRunOwnership`. The card counted two sites at cloud's pin. |
| `runtime/src/app-plugin.ts` (the gate for `defineStack({ jobs })`) | Still reads the deployment resolver. It is not in the ruled shape, and I did not add a surface there. See the acceptance notes. |
| `cli/src/commands/doctor.ts` | Still reads the deployment resolver. `doctor` inspects the deployment's configuration and has no kernel options. |

## Tests (all at `817d4d38f2`)

- **Acceptance test:** `packages/triggers/trigger-schedule/src/per-kernel-scheduled-work-policy.test.ts`. It boots two real `LiteKernel`s in one process, each with the real `AutomationServicePlugin`, `ScheduleTriggerPlugin` and `TimeRelativeTriggerPlugin`. The kernel built with `enabled: false` schedules nothing: no plain `schedule` flow and no `time_relative` sweep reach the job service, and its audit gives `SCHEDULED_WORK_DISABLED_REASON` for both flows. Its sibling built with `enabled: true` schedules both jobs. The test runs under the deployment switch OFF and again under it ON, which shows the per-kernel answer wins over the environment in both directions. Two pins check that the zero-argument path is unchanged: a kernel with no policy follows the deployment in each state. The file also drives both triggers directly, without an engine, with a value and with a resolver.
- **Engine source pins:** `packages/services/service-automation/src/per-kernel-scheduled-work-policy.test.ts`. They cover two engines under both deployment states, the policy reason with no trigger registered, a resolver that is read at each bind, and the zero-argument path (no option, `{}`, `{ scheduledWorkPolicy: undefined }`). They also cover the plugin forwarding, with two kernels plus a control kernel under a deployment that is ON.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/trigger-schedule test`: 6 files, 144 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 142 files, 1696 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/trigger-schedule --filter @objectstack/service-automation typecheck`: both passed. The new trigger-schedule test file appears in `tsc --listFiles`, and service-automation's `check:test-typecheck` is green.
- Targeted eslint (`eslint --no-inline-config --format json`) on the 10 changed TS files: 10 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. None of them was ignored, because an ignored file would show up as a warning. `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting: there is no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, which `--print-config` confirms. So this diff cannot change the lint result of any file it does not touch.

### Ablations (committed first, mutated with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, restored to the HEAD blob with a clean `git diff HEAD`)

1. In `engine.ts`, `readScheduledWorkPolicy` was changed to ignore the option. The engine suite went from 6/6 passing to 5 failing and 1 passing. The zero-argument pin stayed green, as it should.
2. In `schedule-trigger.ts`, `readScheduledWorkPolicy` was changed to ignore `source`. The trigger-schedule suite went from 6/6 passing to 3 failing and 3 passing. The failures were the two direct-trigger cases and the acceptance case under deployment OFF, where the ON kernel's triggers then refuse what its engine allowed.

### Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 61 families, and all 61 were run. Reconciled with `--ran` including exit codes: 59 passed. 2 are NOT MEASURED because the prerequisite is not met (exit 3, both need a whole-workspace build that CI does): `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `pnpm check:type-check-debt`. Neither package is in the debt ledger. The CI jobs and type-check lanes that the derivation lists separately are left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **Plugin forwarding.** The ruling names `AutomationEngineOptions`. Hosts build the engine through `AutomationServicePlugin`, so the option is useless per kernel unless the plugin forwards it. The plugin forwards it the same way it already forwards `maxLogSize` and `runSummaryLog`.
- **Pass the same policy to the engine and both trigger plugins.** Each trigger keeps its own gate for hosts that drive it without the engine. If a trigger reads a different answer from its engine, the engine's audit reports the trigger's refusal as a binding failure. The option docblocks say this.
- **Invariant for hand-built policies.** A hand-built value must keep `requiresActingOrganization === (enabled && runOwnership === 'declared')`. If a host spreads the deployment reading and overrides only `enabled`, the result is wrong under an `isolated` posture: a kernel turned ON would bind org-less flows. The option docblocks and the changeset say so. No builder is added, because that would be a surface outside the ruled shape.
- **Reason text.** The reason is still `SCHEDULED_WORK_DISABLED_REASON` word for word, as ruled. That sentence tells the reader to set `OS_AUTOMATION_SCHEDULED_WORK_ENABLED=true`, which is the wrong fix for a kernel whose host turned it off. This is noted, not changed here.
- **`defineStack({ jobs })`.** Declarative jobs gated in `runtime/src/app-plugin.ts` still follow the deployment switch only. In a mixed-plan host, a kernel whose flows are turned off would still schedule its `defineJob`s while the deployment default is ON. The ruled shape does not cover `AppPlugin`, so this is left for a decision.

Changeset: `minor` for `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/trigger-schedule`, with `Clause-②: no` in its body. No edits under `packages/spec` or `content/docs/releases/**`.
